- **Kyle McCord (QB)** — He is set for his second career start while continuing to fill in for Malik Willis, so Miami’s passing-game projection is still attached to a backup-level quarterback situation rather than a settled starter. That keeps both volume and efficiency risk elevated for the whole offense this week. [1]

- **Chris Bell (WR)** — Bell is back at practice on a limited basis after missing the Colts game, while Jared Wayne remains out and Caleb Douglas was limited with a shoulder issue. If Bell is active, he has the clearest path to reclaim snaps in a thin receiver rotation, making him the Miami pass-catcher most likely to gain projection value. [1, 2]

- **Aaron Brewer (C)** — Brewer missed another practice in concussion protocol, leaving Miami’s center spot uncertain. If he sits, McCord’s interior protection and the run game both take a hit, which would suppress offensive efficiency even if the play volume holds. [1, 2]

- **Bradley Pinion (P)** — Miami signed Jack Browning to the practice squad after Pinion missed practice with a groin injury, so Browning is the contingency if Pinion can’t punt and hold this week. That’s mostly a field-position issue, but it can still affect drive quality for the offense. [2, 6]
